A5_S4_D1: ^Narrator: You take a look at the boat, picking up some of the pieces which have fallen apart and calculating if the toolbox you borrowed would be enough.
^Noelle: Fabric from Clara, wood from the Viridi, some nails and glue…
A5_S4_D2: ^Narrator: With the ship repaired, to at least a rowboat’s level of functionality, you and Amelia celebrate with a treat of berries, discussing where to go next.
^Noelle: Before we try to use it, I want to check the boat again in the morning when it’s bright.
^Noelle: Can’t be too careful, after all. I can swim and allegedly breathe underwater, but you can’t.
^Amelia: Hmph. We dragons live in the mountains after all, so my body isn’t exactly built for paddling.
^Amelia: Should we head back to the Viridi to rest? It’ll be a bit of a walk, but…
choicecampout: ^Noelle: Despite starting my journey here, I never spent that much time on this beach.
^Noelle: What was it that they said… this is where lost things are found?
^Amelia: …Where lost things get stranded, actually, because of the tide.
^Narrator: Amelia seems reluctant, but begrudgingly concedes.
^Amelia: I have lived here for a while, so there’s a small camp to the east.
^Amelia: Just don’t expect anything as cushy as the Viridi or Human’s.
^Narrator: Seeing how quiet the beach is, you can already imagine it’d be a perfect place to gaze at the stars.
^Noelle: Sleeping under the sky is fine with me!
^Amelia: …It’s not that bad! I have a tent like the ones Rowan made.
^Amelia: It’s smaller, though. So don’t complain about the squeeze.
A5_S4_D3: ^Amelia: Ugh… how did it get even messier than before?
^Noelle: That’s alright! Let’s just clean it up.
^Noelle: Even if it’s just for one night, it’d be good to leave the beach in a good condition.
A5_S4_D4: ^Narrator: Being on Thavmia has really made you feel small.

^Narrator: Not in a powerless or insignificant way — but in the sense of realising where you might stand in terms of the island and its inhabitants. As a part of a wider world, which you’ve only just discovered five days ago.
^Narrator: …It’s not so bad, to be honest. There’s a bunch of people of the same size as you.
^Narrator: And smaller, too, like the cotton critter you saved…
^Noelle: (The Great Disaster really must be a huge size, to cause floods all over the Earth.)
^Narrator: Amelia notices you a little lost in thought.
^Amelia: Hey! Noelle, what's with that look? Do you need more supplies from Rowan after all?
^Amelia: So why are you so unhappy?
^Noelle: I’m just thinking about Noah’s story.
^Narrator: Amelia squints at you, realising it’s not sadness, but rather—
^Amelia: Oh, don’t tell me you want to do something crazy!
^Noelle: I’m not going to go and find the Great Disaster or anything!
^Noelle: …It’d be impossible to build a boat for that, in a month’s time.
^Noelle: (But… there’s a feeling in my gut that suggests there’s more to all of this.)
choicehope: ^Noelle: Don’t you think that with the Great Disaster’s size, it could affect more than just the floods?
^Noelle: Even a small breeze can cause stirring in the sea. If it wanted to, surely it could start a storm somewhere that’s normally free from bad weather.
^Noelle: (I’m not saying that the Great Disaster is a villain, but wouldn’t it make sense if it was aiming for Thavmia somehow, as it’s where Noah set up his base?)
^Noelle: (If I was wronged, or perhaps disrespected and angry, I might resort to such actions, too. Knocking on their door.)
^Amelia: Noelle… Even if that were true, and it’s the one causing the storms — you don’t have proof.
^Amelia: And unless the Elders have a magical way to speak to the Kraken that we don’t know about, there’s no way to confirm or appease it either.
^Noelle: …I know. But I can’t put off the feeling that there’s another clue somewhere that just hasn’t been found. Like the box I managed to open for Cillian.
^Narrator: Amelia studies your expression once more.
^Amelia: This is important to you, isn’t it?
^Amelia: Is it because you think Noah might be your ancestor?
^Narrator: A beat passes. You give Amelia a small smile.
^Noelle: I guess… I’d feel like I’ve fulfilled my purpose, if that is the case.
^Noelle: That I washed up here for a reason.
^Noelle: (That I was chased out of home, and fled, for a reason.)
^Amelia: Let’s go back to Rowan’s house and demand for fabric again. And ask Cillian if he’s got any more info before heading to the northern beach.
^Amelia: I’ve heard that the Ichthyos are familiar with seaside caves. Noah probably used them at some point.
^Amelia: But if this search comes up empty, you better be ready to rake up merit points with the settlements!
^Amelia: We are not waiting out the floods outside of the mountains!
A5_S4_D5: ^Noelle: (Oh, and she finally remembered Cillian’s name!)
^Narrator: Before you both head to sleep, Amelia turns back to say something to you, her eyes trained on the campfire.
^Amelia: …As for where I went, while you were decoding artifacts.
^Amelia: I was visiting where my gran and gramps used to live.
^Narrator: You stay silent. Amelia’s tail sways left, then right.
^Amelia: I was the runt of my birth-family, so… as some creatures do, they leave their runts out to fend for themselves.
^Amelia: I was probably meant to grow up wilder, but Gran found me and took me in. She used to live in the human settlement, but her and Gramps retired with a little cottage near the mountains.
^Amelia: They were pretty old for humans, though, so…
^Noelle: (After a while, Amelia must’ve been left alone… again.)
^Amelia: Anyways, that’s why I wandered off today. To tidy up their hut.
^Amelia: Everything’s in place, but I guess the flood will wash it out, soon, so…
^Noelle: Did you want to pick up anything from there? We can definitely bring it up the mountains.
^Amelia: …I’m not sure. I’ll decide after you sort out your big mystery.
^Amelia: Let’s go to bed. Big day of demanding things from the humans tomorrow.
